name: How Many Hospitals Use AI
blurb: Survey data on AI adoption in US hospitals.
title: How Many Hospitals Use AI
answer: Hospital AI use is growing but not yet universal. A national study published in December 2025 found about a third of US hospitals were current AI users and a quarter more planned to adopt within a year. FDA device authorization counts measure what is allowed on the market, not what hospitals actually use.

reading.body:
About a third of US hospitals were current AI users as of December 2025, and roughly a quarter more planned to adopt within a year.

That leaves adoption short of universal even after the planned wave lands. The gap between current and planned users is the number to watch, because intent and deployment are not the same thing, and the data does not say how many of the planners will follow through.

Adoption is not evenly spread. It is far higher in large systems than in small and rural hospitals, so a national rate near a third describes an average that few individual hospitals actually sit at. A small rural hospital reading the headline number should not assume it reflects its own peer group.

FDA device authorization counts are a separate measure. They record what is permitted on the market, not what hospitals run, so they cannot be used to estimate clinical adoption. The data here covers one national survey and one authorization distinction, and does not break adoption down by clinical function, vendor, or spending.
